summary: In the Oracle's apartment, the Priestess tells Morpheus to make himself at home, then takes Neo down a hall into a family room where a woman in white watches a soap opera and half a dozen child Potentials play or meditate. Left to wait, Neo watches a little girl levitate alphabet blocks and a skinny Spoon Boy sway a spoon; he crosses over and sits. The boy hands him a spoon that is now perfectly straight and teaches him, "Don't attempt to warp the spoon. It cannot be done.," urging him to realize "there is no spoon," so that the spoon remains rigid; only you are the one who bends." As Neo stares into the spoon, the whole room reflected in the spoon's reflection gradually starts to curve, at which point a hand on his shoulder interrupts him — the Priestess announces, "The Oracle will see you now," and Spoon Boy smiles.

what_changes.before: A bystander watching the Potentials, he sits beside the Spoon Boy without understanding how the impossible is done.
what_changes.after: He accepts the lesson that bending the spoon is impossible because there is no spoon, so only oneself bends.
what_changes.evidence: NEO: There is no spoon. SPOON BOY

what_changes.before: Left to wait in the family room while the Priestess goes ahead.
what_changes.evidence: A hand touches his shoulder. PRIESTESS: The

event_hint.kind: a teaching / preparation before an audience
event_hint.one_line: While waiting for the Oracle, Neo is taught by Spoon Boy that reality bends only through self-realization, then is called in to see the Oracle.

objects_that_matter: the spoon (swaying, then straight, then bending)
a heap of spoons warped and contorted into knots
the reflected room inside the spoon
uncertain: Whether Morpheus remains in the apartment during Neo's lesson or leaves the room.
Whether Neo's spoon-bending is real within the world or a subjective vision.
The identity and role of the woman in white watching the soap opera.

minds.wants: To find some footing — any way of understanding this world — before he is taken to a woman who claims to know his fate.
minds.feels: Raw and defensive from the hallway (he just told Morpheus he believes in nothing anymore), suspended between the terror of being 'The One' and the safety of being a nobody. The spoon lesson lands because it offers him a way of knowing that does not require faith in a prophecy — it requires only turning his attention inward, which is the one thing he still has authority over.
minds.shows: Curiosity and compliance: he crosses over, sits, asks 'What truth?', nods, repeats 'There is no spoon,' and stares until the reflected room bends. He lets himself be taught.
minds.basis: In sc-083 he explicitly renounced belief ('I don't believe in anything anymore'), and here he does not argue or retreat but engages the boy and actually begins to see the spoon/room bend — the first time in the visit he moves toward something rather than backing away (contrast the hovering hand on the door handle in sc-083).

minds.wants: To hand Neo the actual technique — not a trick, but the reorientation that makes tricks possible: stop fighting the world as external and recognize it as a projection of self.
minds.feels: The unhurried confidence of someone who has already crossed this threshold; he is not showing off (he corrects Neo before Neo tries to perform) but initiating. His smile at the end is the quiet satisfaction of a teacher watching a student actually get it, not of a child who fooled a stranger.
minds.shows: Calm instruction and a deliberately staged prop: he lets the spoon sway, hands Neo a now-straight spoon, and withholds the method until Neo names the truth himself. He says nothing about his own power.
minds.basis: He hands Neo a spoon that 'is now perfectly straight' (having bent it without Neo seeing), and his pedagogy — 'Don't attempt to warp the spoon. It's not possible.' — is a correction aimed at someone about to fail by the old rules. His final smile coincides exactly with Neo's perception beginning to shift.

minds.wants: To shepherd this visitor through the Oracle's house with ritual order — Morpheus parked, Neo prepared and announced at the right moment — without breaking the calm the household maintains.
minds.feels: A practiced, ceremonial composure; she treats the impossible (children meditating, levitating blocks) as ordinary domestic routine, which is itself the house's doctrine made visible.
minds.shows: Efficient hospitality and timing: 'Make yourself at home, Morpheus,' then she removes Neo from Morpheus's side and returns with the exact line that ends the lesson. The hand on Neo's shoulder is a deliberate, gentle interruption — she lets him reach the bend and then calls him.
minds.basis: She separates Neo from Morpheus (the guide who 'can only show you the door' in sc-083) so Neo must step through alone, and her entrance line arrives precisely as the spoon-bending peaks, framing the moment as something the household anticipated rather than startled her.

minds.wants: To deliver Neo to the threshold and then release him — to do the one thing he said he could do ('I can only show you the door') and no more.
minds.feels: The ache left over from the hallway, where he just confessed that his certainty about Neo is not knowledge but faith, bought at the cost of five earlier failures. Being told to 'make himself at home' while Neo is led away enacts exactly his stated limit: he cannot carry Neo the rest of the way, cannot explain it, can only believe.
minds.shows: A simple 'Thank you' and stillness — he lets Neo be taken out of the room without protest, performing the calm of a man who has handed over the outcome.
minds.basis: In sc-083 Morpheus repeatedly frames himself as only a guide ('Morpheus says he can only point out the door; Neo must walk through it on his own. yourself'; 'All I can do is believe'), and here the staging literalizes that: he stays behind while the Priestess takes Neo forward to do the stepping alone.

connects_back: Neo's renunciation of belief in sc-083 ('I don't believe in anything anymore') — the spoon lesson gives him a mode of knowing that bypasses the faith he just rejected.
Morpheus's 'Morpheus can only reveal the door; one must pass through it alone yourself' (sc-083) — realized physically by leaving Neo with the Potentials while the Priestess leads him on.
Morpheus's shaken certainty about Neo after the five previous candidates (sc-083) — the household's serene certainty here is the counterweight to his confessed doubt.
The approach to the Oracle's door and the 'disturbing sense of inevitability' (sc-083) — the waiting room is the pause before that door opens.
sets_up: ev-021: Neo entering the Oracle having just practiced the idea that the world bends to a shift in self-perception — the frame she uses when she 'tests Neo's perception' rests on the same principle the Spoon Boy taught.

ev-021: The Oracle's prophecy that Neo must choose between his own life and Morpheus's — the lesson 'The spoon does not bend; only you do.' is the seed of the self-overcoming that lets him later refuse the choice.
ev-026/ev-024: Neo's eventual willingness to act on belief rather than reason (rescuing Morpheus, his resurrection) is prefigured by his accepting a truth he cannot reason his way into.
dramatic_function: It converts the abstract faith Morpheus demanded in the hallway into a felt, first-person experience: before the Oracle tests Neo's perception, a child teaches him that reality is not fixed 'out there' but responsive to the self — so the scene is the story's first concrete demonstration of the rule Neo will have to live by, and it lets him accept it voluntarily rather than be told to believe it.
